title: Free City of Danzig
capsule: The Free City of Danzig (Freie Stadt Danzig / Wolne Miasto Gdańsk) was a semi-autonomous city-state under League of Nations protection established by the Treaty of Versailles in November 1920, encompassing the Baltic port and surrounding territory at the mouth of the Vistula with a predominantly German-speaking population of about 400,000. Poland was granted special customs and transit rights through the city, creating sustained structural tension between the Polish government, the local German-majority Senate, and successive League of Nations High Commissioners. After years of Nazi penetration of local government through the NSDAP, the German battleship Schleswig-Holstein's bombardment of the Polish garrison at Westerplatte on 1 September 1939 opened the Second World War; the Free City was annexed to the Reich the same day and incorporated into the Reichsgau Danzig-West Prussia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Free City's borders were formally defined under international law and are well-documented; the dataset attestation extends to 1940, consistent with the German annexation period before the post-war restoration of the city as Polish Gdańsk.
